statement: The function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail) such that: (1) len(r) = m and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(r[i]) = n; (2) r is a permutation of the rows of score: there exists a bijection π from {0,...,m-1} to {0,...,m-1} such that for all i with 0 <= i < m, r[i] = score[π(i)]; (3) for all i, j with 0 <= i < j < m, r[i][k] > r[j][k].
preconditions: Let m = len(score) and n = len(score[0]). Assume: - m >= 1 and n >= 1; - for all i with 0 <= i < m, len(score[i]) = n; - k is an integer with 0 <= k < n; - for all i, j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= score[i][j] <= 100000; - all elements of score are distinct: for any (i1,j1) != (i2,j2) with 0 <= i1,i2 < m and 0 <= j1,j2 < n, score[i1][j1] != score[i2][j2].
